name: MJSynth: Synthetic Word Dataset for Scene Text Recognition
description: MJSynth (also known as the Synthetic Word Dataset or Syn90k) is a foundational large-scale synthetic dataset for training deep learning models for natural scene text recognition. Created by the Visual Geometry Group (VGG) at the University of Oxford and introduced by Jaderberg et al. in 2014, MJSynth comprises approximately 8.9 million synthetically generated word image crops spanning an English vocabulary of 90,000 dictionary words. Images are generated through a sophisticated rendering pipeline that applies realistic fonts, border/shadow styling, 3D projective perspective distortion, natural background blending, and Gaussian blur, serving as the industry standard pre-training corpus for CRNN and attention-based scene text recognition models.
